killed_technologies.name: Porous Media Enhanced Heat Transfer
killed_technologies.reason: KILLED: KILLED. The single most dangerous surviving objection is the physics kill: Darcy's law as cited is invalid at the stated Re > 4000 operating point, and the realistic ΔP penalty for any porous insert that delivers meaningful Nu enhancement makes the technology thermodynamically inferior to the established alternatives (nanofluids, finned tubes) documented in the prior art.

killed_technologies.name: Neural Network Based MPPT Control
killed_technologies.reason: KILLED: KILLED. The most dangerous surviving objection is the self-defeating evidence: the candidate's own cited IEEE Access 2023 record (doi:10.1109/access.2023.3291339) already implements the exact proposed intervention, eliminating novelty and leaving the 10-20% efficiency claim as the only differentiator — a claim that is physically impossible against any properly functioning traditional MPPT baseline, given the P_max = G·A·η ceiling.

killed_technologies.name: Electrical Signature Analysis
killed_technologies.reason: KILLED: KILLED. The single most dangerous surviving objection is prior_art: doi:10.1109/eic63069.2025.11123235 and doi:10.1109/eic63069.2025.11123384 directly teach electrical signature analysis for wind turbine defect detection in 2025, destroying the novelty claim that the candidate's "unexploited phenomenon" rests upon — even if every other surface were repaired, the technology is already in the public domain.

killed_technologies.name: Discontinuous PWM Loss Reduction
killed_technologies.reason: KILLED: KILLED. The most dangerous surviving objection is that the candidate's own Esw equation shows the absolute switching-loss benefit of DPWM is smallest precisely at the light loads (0.3-0.6 pu) where the candidate claims it is most effective — meaning the predicted 20-40% reduction can only be expressed as a *fractional* metric at low load, which translates into a negligible absolute wattage saving in an EV traction inverter whose thermal budget is dominated by full-load operation.

killed_technologies.name: Data-Driven Thermal Prediction Model
killed_technologies.reason: KILLED: KILLED. The single most dangerous surviving objection is prior-art self-cancellation: the candidate's own evidence record [doi:10.1016/j.applthermaleng.2026.132277] is identical in mechanism, intervention, application, and effect to what is being proposed, leaving no defensible novelty basis.

killed_technologies.name: Acoustic-Actuated Honeycomb Battery Cooling
killed_technologies.reason: KILLED: KILLED. The single most dangerous surviving objection is that the killer experiment conflates thermal uniformity (a geometric/ballast effect) with acoustic-streaming-driven convection, making the proposed test incapable of falsifying the mechanism even if the underlying physics is wrong — and the underlying physics IS wrong, as energy-balance constraints and Helmholtz resonator Q-factors independently demonstrate.

killed_technologies.name: Stochastic MRR Modeling
killed_technologies.reason: KILLED: KILLED. The single most dangerous surviving objection is prior-art anticipation — six independent CMP records (notably doi:10.31274/etd-180810-313 and doi:10.1016/b978-0-12-821791-7.00099-x) already teach MRR-variation modeling for CMP process control with richer mechanistic content, so even if the equation were salvaged the intervention offers no defensible novelty against incumbent FDC/R2R stacks.

killed_technologies.name: Adaptive Control Reactor Optimization
killed_technologies.reason: KILLED: KILLED. The single most dangerous surviving objection is that the equations provide no controller dynamics, so the claimed 40–70% waste reduction is mathematically ungrounded — the candidate cannot be validated, falsified, or scaled from the stated mathematics alone, and any pilot implementation would be a fishing expedition rather than a test of a quantified prediction.

killed_technologies.name: Cryogenic Cooling Enhancement
killed_technologies.reason: KILLED: KILLED. The single most dangerous surviving objection is the boundary-condition inversion (Surface 6): the candidate's own stated materials (SS304, Ti-6Al-4V) contradict its own stated effectiveness rule, which means even if the underlying effect were real, the targeting logic for the buyer (precision machining of thermally sensitive alloys) is self-defeating.

killed_technologies.name: Amino Acid-Mediated CO2 Conversion
killed_technologies.reason: KILLED: KILLED. The single most dangerous surviving objection is the prior-art overlap: doi:10.1021/acs.energyfuels.5c04026 already teaches amino-acid-mediated CO2 conversion to solid carbonate at industrial scale, reducing the candidate to a routine glycine-for-generic-amino-acid substitution that cannot sustain a defensible novelty or freedom-to-operate position.

killed_technologies.name: Direct Air Capture with Thermal Integration
killed_technologies.reason: KILLED: KILLED. The single most dangerous surviving objection is that the underlying physics (heat integration in DAC) is real and partially effective — the candidate is killed by lack of novelty, lack of primary evidence, and unquantified prediction, but a more rigorously specified version (with specific sorbent, defined ΔT, and a credible 10-20% range rather than 25-40%) could legitimately wound the problem statement.
